body:
Parent: #245. **Blocked by #248:** begin this implementation and its qualification only after #248's limit-free, Commit-time final-delta path has passed its exact-root, >4,096-run, bounded-memory, and failure-custody gates. Reuse those receipts as evidence; do not rerun or relabel a benchmark arm to make this issue pass. This is the concurrency validation and daemon enablement that follows #248, not a rewrite of package E/F or #248.

**Owner ruling (2026-09-26):** Remove the fixed 30-second *whole-shell* `WorkspaceApi::exec` deadline. An admitted command runs until its process group exits or its caller explicitly cancels, disconnects, or the Workspace/daemon shuts down. Elapsed wall time alone must not kill it. Keep bounded output capture, resource admission, per-FUSE-syscall deadlines, Commit deadlines, and repository benchmark timing gates distinct from this command-lifetime policy. Current SDK, Bridge, native transport, and daemon all enforce the 30-second deadline, so changing one constant is insufficient.

## Goal

One sandbox daemon owns **multiple simultaneously mounted Workspaces** against its configured Store. Each Workspace admits **multiple independent, concurrent `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls** running arbitrary `/bin/sh -c` commands. There is no fixed per-daemon, per-Workspace or lifetime Exec-command count: admitted commands consume actual PID, FD, memory and output resources, and finished leases are released. No scan or retained record of all earlier Exec calls is part of admission. The **only logical serialization rule** is **one Commit/Stage submission at a time per Workspace**. Different Workspaces may Commit concurrently when the Store resource budget admits them; there is no daemon-wide Commit mutex. A Commit freezes G1 while accepted mounted writes enter G2, and the next Commit uses the preceding saved head as its base. Commands are concurrent processes, not whole-command transactions: a shell command's syscalls may straddle a capture boundary.

```text
one sandbox daemon, resource-admitted control sessions
  |
  +-- workspace A (id + incarnation, mount A)
  |     exec A1 ---------+
  |     exec A2 ---------+--> concurrent FUSE operations, atomic local publication
  |     Commit A: one G1 capture/Branch publication; later writes go to G2
  |     second Commit A: refused while A's submission remains
  |
  +-- workspace B (different id + incarnation, mount B)
        exec B1 ---------------------> independent mount and command output
        Commit B: own submission; shared Store writer budget still applies
```

## Why the current source cannot do this

- `WorkspaceHost` already has a charged attachment registry and per-ID mount/backing paths, and the SDK owner records multiple Workspace bindings. The sandbox launcher currently sets `LAYERFS_WORKSPACE_MAX_COUNT=2`. But the daemon lifecycle owns only one `selected` Workspace and one `MountHandle`; a second live mount is not exposed. Sibling #219 owns the operator-facing `max_workspaces_per_sandbox` creation policy. The daemon creates Workspaces internally through `WorkspaceHost::attach`; #249 replaces its singleton lifecycle without inventing another Workspace-count knob.
- The daemon admits one control session (Q=0), and dispatch holds its single lifecycle mutex through the complete `exec` process or Commit. A second independent SDK `exec`, or an `exec` plus Commit, therefore cannot enter concurrently. A shell's own child processes can already overlap through one mount, but that is not concurrent `WorkspaceApi::exec` support.
- The shared Workspace host has one `frozen` admission flag, one remote-operation gate, one metadata writer gate, and one outbound service-session mutex. Several filesystem paths still use immediate `writer()` refusal, surfaced to POSIX as `EBUSY`. These are real contention/forward-progress limits even after opening control sessions.
- Process, mount, and failure custody currently rely on single-owner exclusion. Merely changing the session count could let unmount/shutdown discard an active command or a retained Commit outcome.

## Implementation shape

1. Replace the daemon's singleton selected/mount slot with a bounded registry keyed by **Workspace ID + incarnation**. Each entry owns its native Workspace, mount handle, lifecycle state, active-command leases, and failure custody. Authenticate and resolve the exact entry under a short registry lock; release that lock before shell execution, Store I/O, Commit, or unmount waits. An unrelated Workspace must not be excluded by another entry's long command.
2. Admit authenticated control connections and Exec leases by actual PID, FD and memory availability, with no fixed numeric Exec limit per daemon, Workspace or lifetime. Use one event-driven command supervisor (or a small fixed set shared by all commands) for sockets, nonblocking stdout/stderr pipes and child-exit notification; do not allocate a dedicated OS thread, 2 MiB stack or periodic polling loop for each Exec. Each active Exec owns only a small keyed lease, one process group, its required FDs, bounded output buffers, request/response identity and cleanup state: `O(Q)` charged live state for `Q` active commands, with `O(1)` admission/retirement and no work proportional to completed commands. Let OS process creation and sandbox quotas return precise resource refusal; do not replace a count cap with a hidden queue or automatic replay. Preserve per-Workspace authorization and exact incarnation checks.
3. Keep the **per-Workspace submission slot** as Commit/Stage serialization. A second same-Workspace Commit refuses `Busy` while the first is retained; no duplicate C5 publication. Different Workspaces may make progress concurrently, subject to the Store's existing writer budget and Branch expected-head checks. Move a shared host-wide `frozen`/remote gate only where its scope incorrectly blocks this contract; do not raise construction workers or Store quotas to conceal contention. For two Workspaces targeting one Branch, a moved head is an explicit conflict, never a silent merge or retry.
4. Audit mounted operations for short `writer()` collisions under two commands. Wait only within each FUSE callback's own deadline for ordinary short gate holds; retain precise `Busy` for actual unavailable ownership and preserve per-syscall atomicity. The shell itself has no elapsed-time deadline. In particular, create/rename/remove/write and read paths must not turn routine parallel commands into unexplained `EBUSY`.
5. Unmount/close of one Workspace must refuse or wait while its commands, FUSE callbacks, or Commit own it; other Workspaces remain available. Daemon shutdown retains every incomplete mount/process/Commit owner and reports a bounded failure rather than dropping or guessing custody. Keep the existing 4 GiB file, backing, session/output, and Store budgets; this work adds no whole-shell atomicity guarantee or multi-Store routing.

## Deadline-free Exec implementation

- Make the Exec wire request explicitly distinguish **no total execution deadline** from the finite deadlines required by other operations. Update `Request` validation, SDK `control_call`, native client/server transport, daemon dispatch, and shell execution together; do not substitute a very large finite deadline.
- The current daemon checks elapsed time and sends `SIGKILL` to the process group at the 30-second limit. Remove only that whole-command timer. Preserve a process-group owner from spawn through exit and pipe draining, and terminate/reap on explicit cancellation, client disconnect, Workspace teardown, or daemon shutdown. Define the terminal result for each case; never abandon a running child.
- Keep authenticated transport liveness without a total runtime timer. Send bounded-rate heartbeats even when a command writes no files or output. Progress frames must not consume a small lifetime response-frame allowance (currently `frame_budget(0)`), and a blocked/broken connection must be detected and cleaned up. No unbounded resident output or thread/session growth.
- Retain per-FUSE-callback time bounds, Commit deadlines, configured resource quotas, and repository benchmark wall-time gates. Benchmark timing measures and classifies a run; it does not become the product's shell-kill policy. Verify an Exec can exceed the old 30-second boundary without termination and that cancellation/disconnect/teardown still reap the exact process group.

**Resource admission:** Multiple mounted Workspaces and commands are supported in one sandbox. Exec has no fixed count per daemon, Workspace or lifetime; only actual process/FD/memory availability can refuse a new command. Do not introduce a singleton Workspace, global Commit lock, per-Exec worker thread, or a hidden fixed session/handle/cookie/root/arena count below the selected resource policy. Charge live owners to memory, PID, FD, private-backing and Store budgets; reclaim only after their last owner releases. Sibling #219 owns `max_workspaces_per_sandbox`, which caps internally created live Workspaces only, never Exec calls. Its selected value must admit multiple Workspaces for this issue's proof; the launcher's current `2` is not an architectural maximum.

## Post-#248 validation

- Two distinct Workspaces mount simultaneously in one sandbox; independent paths, content roots, commands, status, unmount, and close are correct. A failed/retained attachment consumes capacity until its exact resources are released. Check the selected #219 count policy without a lower hidden singleton cap.
- Two `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls on the **same** Workspace overlap at a deterministic barrier and both return their own exact exit status/stdout/stderr. Another Workspace's command progresses while either is active. With enough resource headroom, increase concurrent calls beyond two on one and several Workspaces; neither daemon nor Workspace has a fixed Exec-count refusal. Run many sequential completed Exec calls and show prompt lease reclamation, bounded resident memory, no cumulative lookup/cleanup scan and no per-command supervisor thread. Record PID/FD/memory and output high-water plus admission/exit cost. Include disjoint writes and a conflicting-path case with explicit per-syscall ordering; do not claim an entire shell command is atomic.
- While one Workspace has overlapping commands, Commit captures G1, later accepted writes remain in G2, and a second sequential Commit publishes only G2 against the first saved head. Run this on the post-#248 final-delta path, with old-head readback and exact bytes/root. A simultaneous second Commit on the same Workspace is refused without a second publication. With Store writer capacity for two, Commits in two different Workspaces overlap and retain distinct outcomes; a shared Branch head conflict is explicit. Shared Store resource refusals are identified as such.
- A short metadata-gate collision in ordinary namespace/file operations does not produce unexplained `EBUSY`; deadline and true capacity refusals remain exact. Report accepted/rejected command and Commit counts, active process/session high-water, mount ownership, and shared Store admission.
- Unmount/close/shutdown during active commands or a retained Commit has deterministic custody: no orphaned child, lost mount, duplicate operation, leaked Workspace binding, or cross-Workspace teardown. Wrong ID/incarnation and unauthorized control requests cannot reach another Workspace.

**Source anchors:** [daemon singleton lifecycle](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/lifecycle.rs), [Q=0 control and long dispatch lock](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/control.rs), [shell process ownership](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/execution.rs), [Workspace host registry and shared gates](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/host.rs), [capture/submission slot](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/overlay/snapshot.rs), [sandbox launch count](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-sandbox/src/docker.rs), [#219 workspace-count policy](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/219).

## Source-audited concurrency and resource model — 2026-09-26

The [architecture/complexity research](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE_COMPLEXITY_RESEARCH.md) at [`7939c56d1`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/7939c56d1) is reviewable in [PR #250](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/250). #249 remains blocked by #248.

At source `74ac30e28`, `WorkspaceHost` has bounded per-ID backing and mount paths, but the daemon still has one selected mount, Q=0 control admission, and a lifecycle lock held through Exec/Commit. FUSE callbacks within one shell can overlap; two independent `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls through the daemon cannot yet overlap. Native `active_operations` counts guarded syscalls and Commit operations, **not a shell between syscalls**. Once the long daemon lock is released, each Workspace needs a command lease from admission before spawn through process-group and output cleanup; unmount/close/shutdown must consult it along with retained Commit custody.

For `V` mounted Workspaces and `Q` admitted commands, target owner state is `O(V+Q)`, plus shell/child RSS, mount threads/FDs, and private pages/payloads. Captured stdout/stderr is currently bounded at 8 KiB each per command; the sandbox's 2 CPU, 512 MiB and 64 PID caps do not prove algorithmic memory or independent throughput. Different Workspaces may still contend on the host-wide remote/metadata gates, outbound transport, Store writer budget, and Branch expected-head checks. Keep one Commit/Stage submission per Workspace and test true two-Exec overlap, an unrelated Workspace, Exec+Commit capture/reconcile, exact response ownership, gate collision, and teardown under active leases with deterministic barriers.
title: Post-#248: concurrent Exec and multiple Workspaces per sandbox with serialized Commit
